title: ReproLog
description: Reproducibility record emitted before any run that writes to artifacts/ or logs/. Composed of 13 core fields plus a 4-field 'runtime' sub-object (2026-05-18 runtime-stack augmentation).
$comment: Core 13-field contract: run_id, phase, hypothesis_id, timestamp_utc, git_head, pip_freeze_sha256, pip_freeze_path, dataset_checksums, rng_seed, model_hash, config_resolved_sha256, host, env_id. The 'runtime' sub-object (python_version, platform, container_digest, os_release) was added 2026-05-18 to capture interpreter/OS/container detail beyond what 'host' carries; rationale per Boettiger (2015), 'An introduction to Docker for reproducible research,' ACM SIGOPS Oper. Syst. Rev. 49(1):71-79, doi:10.1145/2723872.2723882.

phase.description: Suggested values: bootstrap, backtest, inference, validation, deliver. Not enum-constrained for forward compatibility.

hypothesis_id.description: HID (e.g. H055) or 'n/a' for non-hypothesis-bound work

git_head.description: 40-hex SHA of HEAD, or 'unknown' if outside a git repo

pip_freeze_sha256.description: Full 64-hex SHA-256 of pip-freeze stdout. NOT a truncated cache digest.

pip_freeze_path.description: Project-relative POSIX path to the captured freeze text

rng_seed.description: Explicit seed used; 0 if no sampling

model_hash.description: Model commit / weight SHA when applicable

config_resolved_sha256.description: SHA-256 of resolved config snapshot (e.g., frozen design.md content). Null when no config attached; 64-hex string when set - empty string is not valid.

python.description: platform.python_version() output, e.g. '3.12.1' - version only, NOT interpreter path

host.description: Compact host triple. For finer-grained interpreter/OS/container info see the 'runtime' sub-object.

runtime.description: Runtime-stack sub-object added 2026-05-18 for finer-grained execution-environment capture beyond the compact 'host' triple.
runtime.$comment: Rationale: Boettiger (2015), 'An introduction to Docker for reproducible research,' ACM SIGOPS Oper. Syst. Rev. 49(1):71-79, doi:10.1145/2723872.2723882, argues that recreating a computational result requires not just the source-code version and library list but the operating-system distribution, kernel version, and (when applicable) container image digest. The 'host' field's truncated python_version() output, system()/release() string, and machine() string are insufficient: the same library list under Ubuntu 22.04 vs Alpine 3.19 can produce divergent floating-point results due to glibc vs musl, different BLAS backends, and different threading defaults. The four fields below capture: full interpreter banner (sys.version), the composite platform string (platform.platform()), the container image digest when running inside Docker/Podman/Kubernetes (null otherwise), and the OS-release identifier read from /etc/os-release on Linux or platform.win32_ver()/platform.mac_ver() on Windows/macOS.

python_version.description: sys.version output - full Python interpreter version string including build/compiler info (typically 3+ lines worth concatenated by Python at startup)

platform.description: platform.platform() output - single-string composite (system + release + version + machine)

container_digest.description: Docker/Podman image SHA-256 digest when running inside a container; null when no container is detected or the digest cannot be read. Detection probes /.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, /proc/self/cgroup, and the KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST / DOCKER_CONTAINER env vars.

os_release.description: OS-release identifier. Linux: PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release. Windows: platform.win32_ver() joined with spaces. macOS: platform.mac_ver() joined with spaces. Empty string if no source is readable.
